messages:
maria: Heads-up, thinking through envelope encryption for the inference runtime. Questions around DEK/KEK split, how aggressive should we be with KMS calls, and a safe cache invalidation/rotation pattern. Anyone ran this at scale?

alex: We did a version for Dedicated last year. TL;DR: DEKs cached locally, KEKs only used to unwrap on miss or rotation. But frequency and TTL depend on traffic and KMS quotas.

kris: Important to call out cross-cloud differences: AWS KMS has envelope helpers and CloudTrail; GCP CMEK uses IAM bindings and audit logging in Cloud Audit Logs; Azure Key Vault has RBAC + diagnostic logs to monitor usage.

maria: For AWS specifically, what's a realistic cache TTL? 1h? 10m? tradeoffs?

alex: We used a two-tier cache: process-local DEK cache with TTL ~10m and a shared redis/consensus layer for warm-up with TTL ~1h. On miss, unwrap KEK via KMS, then refresh local cache. Add jitter to TTL to avoid stampedes.

jonah: Also watch KMS request throttles. AWS has limits per-region (and per-key). Clients should implement exponential backoff + circuit breaker. In high QPS paths, aim to keep unwraps <1% of requests.

kris: Sketch of unwrap path:
```
if local_cache.has(key_id):
  use DEK
else:
  DEK = redis_cache.get(key_id)
  if DEK: populate local_cache
  else:
    DEK_wrapped = metadata_store.fetch_wrapped_dek(key_id)
    DEK = KMS.unwrap(DEK_wrapped, kek_id)
    redis_cache.set(key_id, DEK_wrapped, ttl=3600)
    populate local_cache
```
This keeps KMS calls only when metadata changes or cache misses.

maria: For rotation: when KEK rotates (new key version), we need to rewrap DEKs with the new KEK. How to do without mass KMS ops?

alex: We use lazy rewrap + background async rewrap. On first unwrap after rotation, rewrap DEK with new KEK and write new wrapped blob. Background job scans and rewraps remaining DEKs. Metrics to track remaining fraction.

kris: Add a short-lived "rekey marker" in object metadata so clients know they might need to rewrap on next access. That avoids a thundering herd.

jonah: Incident scenario: suspected KEK compromise. Playbook: 1) disable KEK (deny decrypt) 2) enable emergency KEK/rotation key 3) stop accepting new unwraps from compromised key by updating metadata pointer -> new KEK 4) start rewrap job on objects still pointing at old KEK 5) revoke any service principals that had KEK privileges and rotate credentials.

maria: If we disable KEK decrypt immediately, but DEKs are only wrapped by that KEK, how do we serve traffic during rewrap?

alex: Two approaches: a) fallback to cached DEKs (honor local caches for a short window while rewrap progresses), b) allow a "read-only" emergency decrypt role that is heavily audited and time-limited. Both are risky; prefer minimizing window by prioritizing rewrap jobs and throttling traffic to critical paths.

maria: Audit logging requirements? need to capture unwrap/rewrap and service principals used.

kris: Log everything: KMS API events (CloudTrail / Audit Logs / KeyVault diagnostics), application-level logs with key_id, principal, request_id, and a hash of DEK metadata (no plaintext). Ship to SIEM and alert on anomalies: surge in decrypts, decrypts from unexpected regions, or failed decrypt spikes.

sec-bot: Reminder: ensure KEK admin role is separate from application roles. Principle of least privilege + MFA for manual ops. :rotating_light:

jonah: RBAC notes per provider: AWS - grant kms:Decrypt only to the inf service role scoped to the key, use condition on encryption_context; GCP - use IAM roles (cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt) and service account constraints; Azure - separate RBAC role assignments for wrap/unwrap and management operations.

maria: Thoughts on storing DEKs in redis vs local FS? durability vs blast radius?

alex: Redis (encrypted at rest + access controls) is fine as a shared warm cache; avoid single-process local fs for fleets. For per-host hot cache, keep ephemeral in memory only. Always encrypt transit and set short TTLs.

kris: One more: include a cache-coherency invalidation channel. When a DEK is rewrapped, publish an event so nodes drop local DEK and fetch the new wrapped blob. That avoids serving with old KEK after rotation.

maria: OK actionable summary for a playbook?

jonah: 1) Default: client-local DEK cache (TTL 5-15m) + shared redis warm cache (TTL 30-90m) 2) KMS unwrap only on cache miss + exponential backoff and CB 3) Lazy rewrap + background full rewrap job on rotation 4) Invalidate local caches via event bus on rewrap 5) Strong audit pipeline for KMS events + app logs 6) Strict RBAC for KEK ops and emergency rotation runbook 7) Alert on decrypt spike / region anomalies 8) Test the rotation playbook in drills

maria: Perfect. Can someone add a short checklist for the runbook and link to the rewrap utility?

alex: I'll drop a PR with the runbook and our rewrap lambda/worker example later today.

devops-oncall: I'll add KMS quota dashboards and alerting for decrypt rate per-key.

maria: Thanks all — this is enough to start drafting the design doc and incident-runbook.

kris: FYI we'll also want to coordinate with Compliance for retention of decrypt audit logs for 1yr per policy.

maria: noted. Closing thread after doc PR lands. :white_check_mark:
